outlook: Soybeans closed up 7¾ cents Thursday, ending an eight-session losing streak, as crude oil jumped on reports of damaged tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and strong export sales of about 2.8 million tons plus a 202,000-ton flash sale to China. Corn slipped 2¾ cents under harvest pressure despite solid export sales, while wheat fell again — Minneapolis December down 9¾ cents — on growing hopes for a Russia-Ukraine peace deal and weak wheat export sales. Overnight into Friday, corn was about 2 cents lower and wheat and soybeans near unchanged as traders squared positions ahead of the weekend, with crude oil higher on renewed U.S.-Iran tensions. November soybean options expire today, and rain is moving into parts of the Midwest after a long stretch of good harvest weather.
